# PolicyLens

> PolicyLens reads a health insurance policy and works out what the insurer should pay for a claim. A language model extracts the coverage terms, each with a page number and a verbatim quote. A fixed Decimal rules engine, with no model in it, calculates the payout and returns an audit trail. It is an open-source portfolio demo, not insurance, legal or financial advice.

Key facts for anyone summarising or citing this project:

- The model only reads. It never calculates money. The payout comes from deterministic code: waiting period, exclusions, room rent cap, ICU cap, sub-limit, deductible, co-payment, sum insured.
- Every extracted value carries its source page and quote; the server checks the quote appears on the cited page and flags weak values for a person.
- Synthetic sample policies only. Insurers in the samples are fictional.
- Reading a policy uses a paid model, so extraction is rate limited. Estimating a claim uses no model.
- Eval numbers on the site come from one run on 10 synthetic policies written by the author; treat them as an upper bound.

## Project

- [Repository and README](https://github.com/Zoronium/policylens): what it does, how to run it, the API, evals and limitations
- [Rules engine assumptions](https://github.com/Zoronium/policylens/blob/main/engine/README.md): the simplified model of a policy the payout uses
- [Deployment guide](https://github.com/Zoronium/policylens/blob/main/docs/DEPLOY.md): environment variables and hosting notes

## API

- `POST /policies`: multipart `file` (PDF or text) or `text`; returns extracted coverage with citations
- `GET /policies/{id}`: a stored policy
- `POST /estimate`: `{policy_id, scenario}`; returns the payout and audit trail
- `GET /samples`: the synthetic sample policies

## Optional

- The site's privacy policy is at `/#/privacy` on the deployed site.
